html:
An oil pipeline built from 1947 to 1950 to carry oil from the eastern oil fields of Saudi Arabia across the desert to the port of Sidon in Lebanon, on the Mediterranean. It was over 1,200 kilometres long.

The American oil company Aramco, later Saudi Aramco, had the line built so that tankers bound for Europe would not have to sail round Arabia and pay to pass the Suez Canal. It ran through Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Syria and Lebanon, and each country was paid transit fees. Its pumping stations became small towns in the desert, and in Lebanon it brought jobs and money.

Politics wore it down. Sabotage and fights over fees with Syria shut it more than once, and after the war of 1967 its route crossed the Golan Heights, which Israel now held. Supertankers made the long route cheaper. Flows to Lebanon stopped in 1976, early in the civil war, and the remaining link to Jordan ended in 1990.
sum: An oil pipeline built from 1947 to 1950 to carry oil from the eastern oil fields of Saudi Arabia across the desert to the port of Sidon in Lebanon, on the Mediterranean. It was over 1,200 kilometres long.
